title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'troisième mouture' of Analysis situs (June 1986), Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, point-free 'tame' topology. The data are a set M of objects (closed 'pieces', e.g. tame closed sets or polyhedra) with:
- a partial order Y ≪ X, read 'Y is in the shadow of X';
- Omb(X) = {Y : Y ≪ X};
- a boundary operator ∂X;
- a restriction Y_Z (also written Y|Z), the 'trace' of Y on Z;
- a disjointness relation Y ∥ Z;
- a family X̃ of 'reductions' or pieces X' of X, with X' < X or X' ≤ X.
Axioms referred to on this page are D0 and the 'Ar'/'L' axioms L1–L3, plus divisibility and non-emptiness axioms.

Definition. The interior of X is X° = {Y ∈ Omb(X) : Y ∥ ∂X}. Equivalent forms given:
- Y_{∂X} = ∅;
- Ỹ ∩ Omb(∂X) = ∅, i.e. no piece of Y lies in the shadow of the boundary.
This X° is the earlier Omb°°(X) of p.88, which is contained in Omb°(X) = Omb(X) \ Omb(∂X). X° is thus a downward-closed family (a 'partie fermée par ≪' of M) representing the open interior of X, given as the set of closed pieces it contains. Disjointness extends to such families: X° ∥ Y° means X' ∥ Y' for all X' ∈ X°, Y' ∈ Y°.

Warning (boxed, right). X° ∩ Y° = ∅ does NOT imply X° ∥ Y°. Taking 'points' x, y for X, Y, that implication would force all distinct points to be disjoint, which the framework must not impose (generic or non-separated points, or the non-Boolean nature of ∥).

Lemma 1. X ∥ Y ⇔ for all X' ∈ X̃, Y' ∈ Ỹ, X'° ∥ Y'°. In words: two pieces are disjoint iff the interiors of all their pieces are disjoint.
- ⇒: trivial, since X'° ⊂ Omb(X') ⊂ Omb(X), and similarly for Y, plus axiom D0 (disjointness is inherited by shadows).
- ⇐: 'less clear'. It is reduced, as on p.88, to L2 and L3 via a pointwise criterion: X ∥ Y iff x ∥ y for all points x ∈ omb(X), y ∈ omb(Y). The margin adds a corollary: X ∥ Y ⇔ ∀Y' ∈ Ỹ, X ∥ Y'°.

Lemma 2 (assuming L1, L2, L3). Let Y ≪ X.
- (a) Y° ⊂ X° iff Y °≪ X. Here Y °≪ X means Y meets ∂X only inside its own boundary: Y_{∂X} ≤ ∂Y.
- (b) Y °°≪ X, i.e. Y ∈ X°, iff Y'° ⊂ X° for all Y' ∈ Ỹ.

Proof of (a) ⇒, begun here and finished on p.90. Take Y' ∈ Y°, so Y' ≪ Y and Y' ∥ ∂Y; then Y' ≪ X by transitivity. Next, Y'_{∂X} = Y'|(Y_{∂X}) ≤ Y'|∂Y = ∅, so Y' ∈ X°. The converse on p.90 uses non-emptiness of interiors (from L1 plus divisibility) to get a contradiction Z ∥ Z.

Purpose: the page sets up a calculus of interiors versus closed pieces. The aim is to express disjointness, and later 'relative interior / manifold-with-boundary' notions, in purely order-theoretic terms inside an axiomatic tame topology. This belongs to the Esquisse §5 programme of a 'topologie modérée' based on axioms on a class of closed pieces rather than on open sets.
errors: The last 'i.e.' in the definition of X° ('∃ Y' ≤ Y, Y' ≪ X' < X') reads literally as the negation of the preceding conditions. It is presumably meant as '∄' or 'non ∃', or the relation symbol is garbled; as written it is inconsistent with Ỹ ∩ Omb(∂X) = ∅.

Lemma 1 ⇐ is not proved on the page. It is only asserted to follow from L2, L3 via a pointwise criterion, and the remark 'OK sans même ... L2, L3' and the crossed-out text leave unclear which axioms are really needed.

Lemma 2(a) ⇒ silently uses transitivity of ≪ and the restriction compatibility Y'_{∂X} = Y'|(Y_{∂X}), an axiom of 'induction' made explicit only on p.90. Monotonicity of Y'|(·) in the second argument is also used.
The boxed warning is correctly flagged: disjointness as families (∩ = ∅) and the relation ∥ must not be conflated.

ideas.what: Interior of a closed piece defined as the family of its shadows disjoint from its boundary; open sets represented as ≪-downward-closed families of closed pieces
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / mereotopological interior; ideals of a lattice of closed (tame) sets; regular-closed region algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereotopology: Whitehead, de Laguna, Clarke (1981), Randell–Cohn–Cui RCC (1992). Point-free topology: Wallman, Stone, locale theory
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984), without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Lemma 1: two pieces are disjoint iff interiors of all their pieces are pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: Separation via interiors in a stratified / o-minimal or polyhedral setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore for polyhedra and definable sets

ideas.what: Lemma 2: for Y ≪ X, interior inclusion Y° ⊂ X° iff Y meets ∂X only within ∂Y; Y ⊂ int X iff all pieces' interiors lie in int X
ideas.modern_name: Relative interior / boundary compatibility of subcomplexes (face-of-boundary condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of PL topology and stratified spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics (part order ≪, boundary ∂, disjointness ∥, interior as a family of closed parts) is in effect a mereotopology with an explicit boundary operator, developed independently of and in parallel with the Whitehead/Clarke/RCC tradition in philosophical logic and AI. That literature has never been compared with his tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: X° = { Y ∈ Omb(X) | Y ∥ ∂X i.e. Y_{∂X} = ∅ }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A comparison could give a ready-made axiom system for 'tame' region-based topology (o-minimal and PL regions) and test which of his axioms (L1–L3, divisibility) correspond to known mereotopological ones. It is of modest interest, since the content of this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine development of definitions and lemmas inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. It is interesting as documentation of the 1986 Analysis situs programme, but the mathematical content (interiors and disjointness) is elementary.
transcription_corrections: The line before 'Donc pour X, Y ∈ M' reads 'on Omb°°(X) ⊂ Omb°(X)': the 'on' is written above, an insertion meaning that X° is the former Omb°°(X).
Lemma 2 layout: 'Soit Y ≪ X. Alors [à préciser] Y° ⊂ X°. On a: a) Y °≪ X ssi [Y° ⊂ X°]; b) Y °°≪ X i.e. Y ∈ X° ssi ∀Y' ∈ Ỹ, Y'° ⊂ X°'. In b) the relation should be ⊂ (as on p.90), not ∈.
'Suppossons' after 'Soit Y ≪ X' is crossed out.
'At Do.' is probably 'Att D0' (axiom D0); 'Att L2, L3' / 'Att L1, L2, L3' denote axiom labels, the 'Ar' axioms of p.88.
Margin: 'NB Y ∈ X° signifie Y ≪ X et Y ∥ ∂X ... X° partie fermée de M, ≪ ...; mieux définir Y ∈ Omb°°(X) ... Y ∈ Omb°(X)'; corollary 'Cor X ∥ Y ⇔ ∀Y' ∈ Ỹ, X ∥ Y'°'.

Boxed remark: 'Attention, prouver aussi que X° ∩ Y° = ∅ ⇒ X° ∥ Y°, cela voudrait dire pour x, y ∈ L, x ≠ y ⇒ x ∥ y ! (pas)'. The word 'prouver' is uncertain and may be 'ne pas croire'; the sense is a warning against the implication.
